turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
My predicted top five are **c030, c038, c044, c097, and c088**, in that order. I prioritize close **complete-device analogues** in the training data, using interface and contact physics to assess the changes. These are predictions of configuration-level median efficiency, not guaranteed measured rankings.

| Rank | Candidate | Training evidence and physical rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **c030** | The corresponding **PCBM-60 / Bphen, PTAA / PMMA, Al** device achieves **19.48%**; c030 adds IDTT2FPDI before PCBM-60. PTAA provides hole selectivity, while a suitably thin PMMA interlayer can suppress interfacial recombination without substantially obstructing extraction. PCBM/Bphen supplies an electron-selective, hole-blocking contact to Al. The added acceptor could improve interfacial extraction or coverage, although its benefit is not established by this dataset. The already strong underlying recipe makes this my first choice. |
| **2** | **c038** | The closest distinctive analogue—**FTO, PCBM-60, Au-np / NiO-c, Ag, spin-coating**—reaches **20.0%**. c038 retains that modified hole-contact stack, changes FTO to ITO, and adds PEI at the electron contact. NiO provides hole selectivity; Au nanoparticles can modify its electrical and optical response, depending on morphology. Thin PEI can create a favorable contact dipole and reduce electron-extraction resistance at Ag. This is promising, but less certain than a nearly unchanged recipe because both the substrate and electron interface change. |
| **3** | **c044** | This has particularly strong support: **PCBM-60 / C60 / BCP, PTAA, Cu, spin-coating** gives **18.85%**, while **C60 / BCP, PTAA, Cu** gives **18.62%** with sequential spin-coating and **19.085%** with slot-die coating. c044 preserves the favorable PTAA–fullerene–BCP–Cu combination. PCBM supports electron extraction and interfacial passivation, while BCP limits hole leakage and separates the fullerene from the metal. Omitting the additional C60 layer introduces some coverage/contact uncertainty. |
| **4** | **c097** | Its sulfur-containing counterpart, **ITCPTC-Th / C60 / BCP, P3CT-Na, Ag, spin-coating**, achieves **18.49%**. The analogous NDP-V stack also reaches **17.585%**, supporting this broader selective-contact combination. Substituting the selenium analogue could alter acceptor energy levels, packing, and mobility, but there is no basis here to assume an automatic improvement. Retaining the same HTL, fullerene buffer, metal, and process nevertheless makes this a strong near-neighbor prediction. |
| **5** | **c088** | The **C60 / BCP, PTAA, Cu** family has the **18.62–19.085%** training results noted above. Doctor-bladed **C60 / BCP, PTAA, Ag** also achieves **16.9%**, demonstrating that this absorber-process/contact family can work well with blading. Willow glass retains a glass/ITO substrate rather than introducing a polymer electrode platform. Its main uncertainty is whether the blade-coated absorber maintains dense coverage and low defect density on that substrate. |

Across these choices, the strongest recurring signal is **selective hole contacts paired with fullerene-based electron extraction and a suitable metal-contact buffer**. These combinations can reduce nonradiative recombination and extraction losses, supporting both voltage and fill factor. I do not assume that extra interlayers or additional deposition steps inherently improve film quality; their thickness, wetting, and chemistry remain important unreported variables.

**Final: c030, c038, c044, c097, c088**
